holidays.name: World Chocolate Day
holidays.description: A sweet celebration dedicated to all things cocoa, from silky truffles to the humble candy bar. Chocoholics around the globe have a perfectly good excuse to indulge.
holidays.origin: Said to have been established in celebration of chocolate's arrival in Europe, with some traditions linking it to the 1550 introduction of chocolate to Europe. It is observed in many countries, though the exact origin is unclear.
holidays.funFact: The Aztecs and Maya valued cacao beans so highly that they were used as currency, meaning chocolate literally did grow on trees as money.

holidays.name: Global Forgiveness Day
holidays.description: A day to let go of grudges, apologize to the people you have wronged, and forgive those who have wronged you. Think of it as spring cleaning for your emotional baggage, in the middle of summer.
holidays.origin: Founded by Dr. Dyer-Fisher-Whyte, as an international observance to promote forgiveness and peace of mind. It is a grassroots observance rather than an official government holiday.
holidays.funFact: Researchers have found that practicing forgiveness is associated with lower stress levels and even better heart health.

holidays.name: Tanabata (Star Festival)
holidays.description: A Japanese festival where people write wishes on colorful strips of paper and hang them on bamboo branches. It celebrates the once-a-year meeting of two star-crossed lovers, the stars Vega and Altair.
holidays.origin: Rooted in a Chinese legend of the weaver girl Orihime and the cowherd Hikoboshi, who were separated by the Milky Way and allowed to meet only on the seventh day of the seventh month. The festival came to Japan centuries ago.
holidays.funFact: If it rains on Tanabata, legend says the lovers cannot cross the Milky Way, so their reunion is postponed until next year.

holidays.name: Macaroni Day
holidays.description: A day for celebrating the humble noodle that powers mac and cheese, pasta salads, and late-night snacks. Break out the elbow pasta and get cheesy.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food holiday observed in the United States, listed among the many food days that celebrate pasta staples.
holidays.funFact: The song Yankee Doodle mentions a feather in a cap called macaroni, which referred to a fashionable 18th-century style, not pasta.

holidays.name: Sugar Plum Day
holidays.description: A tribute to the mysterious confection that dances in everyone's head at Christmastime but arrives in the middle of July. It is a perfect excuse for candied fruit and nostalgic ballet references.
holidays.origin: A quirky unofficial food observance listed on holiday calendars, with no known single founder.
holidays.funFact: Traditional sugar plums are not made from plums at all but are small candies made by coating nuts, seeds, or spices in layers of hardened sugar.
